content:
Maria: Follow-up on the token-broker RFC: this thread is to decide smoothing/decay semantics and the client-facing hint model before the canary. Short notes + questions below.

Arun: quick summary?

Maria: Two parts: 1) how we decay penalty scores / restore credits after bursts (smoothing) 2) what metadata we return to clients on 429s so they can back off gracefully (hints).

Priya: For smoothing: are we thinking leaky bucket with exponential decay or windowed rolling average?

Maria: Leaning to hybrid: leaky-bucket credit accounting, but penalty multiplier decays exponentially with configurable half-life per tenant class. That avoids abrupt cliff restores.

Arun: Why not simple sliding window? easier to reason about.

Maria: sliding window is simpler but brittle when traffic is sparse; exponential gives gradual recovery and smoother UX for clients. We can expose half-life in config so enterprise customers can tweak.

Priya: Need to simulate attack patterns. Small rapid bursts vs long, low-rate abuse show different behaviors. Do we have sim coverage?

Maria: Spike will include three scenarios: micro-bursts (100 reqs/s), slow leak (sustained 10r/s), and coordinated multi-key hammering. We'll run both decay strategies and capture fairness index + time-to-recover.

sre-bot: Reminder: log penalty transitions with reason codes for audit and regression debugging.

Arun: Client hints: what fields? retry-after is obvious but we should include machine-readable tokens remaining and estimated warm-up time.

Priya: How about providing a 'backoff_score' [0..1] that clients can use to choose linear/exponential backoff? Keep hints low-cardinality.

Maria: Proposed 429 body: { code: "quota_exceeded", tokens_remaining: 0, retry_after_seconds: 8, penalty_score: 0.67, sample_rate: 0.01 } where sample_rate tells clients whether we sampled the request for extra diagnostics. All numeric fields are advisory.

Arun: Sampling: we need to tag a small fraction of denials with extra debug context (stack traces, route histograms) and route to secure storage. What sample_rate do we set? 0.1% by default?

Priya: 0.1% sounds fine, but for high-traffic tenants that could be noisy. Maybe sample proportionally to tenant size with an upper cap.

Maria: Agree: adaptive sampling: base_rate + min(max_rate_per_tenant, scale*log(tenant_qps)). Configurable per org. We'll include sample_rate in the 429 body so client SDKs can opt-in to richer telemetry.

infra-bot: Note: ensure sampled payloads are scrubbed of PII before persisting.

Arun: What about 'soft-deny' vs 'hard-deny'? Soft-deny returns small tokens_granted with short expiry for retries, hard-deny is 0 and longer cooldown.

Priya: Soft-deny enables graceful degradation for apps that can queue requests. But could be gamed. We should only soft-deny when penalty_score under threshold and when edge cache indicates transient spike.

Maria: Proposed rules: if tokens_granted > 0 -> response code still 429 but include tokens_granted and shorter retry_after; if tokens_granted == 0 -> long cooldown and reason code. We'll make SDKs treat tokens_granted>0 as allowed degraded path.

Arun: Ops metrics to add before canary: time-to-recover-50/90 per tenant, deny-rate-by-penalty-band, sampled-debug-rate, and fraction of soft-denies vs hard-denies.

sre-bot: Add circuit-breaker thresholds to runbook: if soft-deny fraction > 30% for 5min, auto-revert to local-admit mode in region.

Priya: How do Dedicated customers configure smoothing? via broker config with tenant overrides? They may want no smoothing (instant restore).

Maria: Yes: broker exposes policy layers: global default -> plan-level -> tenant override. Dedicated/Private get config surface; hosted tenants use sane defaults.

Arun: Security: do not leak precise tokens_remaining for enterprise customers who might expose quotas to end-users. Maybe return rounded buckets (e.g., "<10", "<100").

Priya: Good call. Add option to mask hints per tenant policy. SDKs should map masked hints to generic backoff guidance.

Maria: Open questions for the RFC: - default half-life (minutes) per tenant tier - token rounding scheme for hints - soft-deny eligibility heuristics - adaptive sampling function parameters - retention of sampled debug artifacts

Arun: I can run parameter sweeps in the sim next week. Priya will sketch SDK hint handling and masking. Maria please add these open questions to the RFC checklist.

Maria: Will do. Also adding a short example 429 payload to RFC and a snippet for SDK behavior. Example: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "code": "quota_exceeded",
  "tokens_remaining": "<10",
  "retry_after_seconds": 5,
  "penalty_score": 0.42,
  "tokens_granted": 2,
  "sample_rate": 0.001
}
```

Priya: LGTM. Let's keep client hints permissive but optional for privacy-sensitive customers.

sre-bot: Ops: include breadcrumb metrics for caching divergence and broker fail-open count.

Maria: Thanks all. I'll update RFC with these parameter candidates and schedule the sim spike. Tagging @eng-sre for final runbook review.
